method: scripts/ib-research/claim-check.js: the passage is copied verbatim from the live source text at the pinned revision; VERIFIED = every claim number in one sentence that shares >= 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: Near Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity is 9.8 m/s2.
records.passage: Near Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity, accurate to 2 significant figures, is 9.8 m/s2 (32 ft/s2).

records.claim: Gravity on Earth's surface varies by around 0.7%, from 9.7639 m/s2 on Nevado Huascarán to 9.8337 m/s2 at the Arctic Ocean surface.
records.passage: Gravity on the Earth's surface varies by around 0.7%, from 9.7639 m/s2 on the Nevado Huascarán mountain in Peru to 9.8337 m/s2 at the surface of the Arctic Ocean.

records.claim: The conventional value for standard gravity is 9.80665 m/s2, originally adopted by the CGPM in 1901.
records.passage: The conventional value for standard gravity is 9.80665 m⋅s−2‍ by definition, originally adopted by the CGPM in 1901.

records.claim: The weight of an object on Earth's surface is the downward force on it, force equals mass times acceleration.
records.passage: The weight of an object on Earth's surface is the downwards force on that object, given by Newton's second law of motion, or F = m a (force = mass × acceleration).

narration.text: Gravity doubles tomorrow. Your weight doubles too.
Your mass stays the same. Only the pull changes.
Weight is mass times gravity's pull, 9.8 metres per second squared.
Double it, and every step lifts twice the load.
Today, gravity varies across Earth by only about 0.7%.
So a doubling dwarfs every difference you've ever felt.
Your heart would push blood uphill against twice the pull.
So the first strain lands on bodies, not buildings.
